Susan — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Looping in Kimberly (payments/tax) and Ben (commercials) + Jonas from legal ops. A few quick points and an ask for follow-up: 

- Billing entity fallback: we can include a fallback clause that allows Redwood US Inc. to invoice Novaterra NA (our US entity) in the event Novaterra EU cannot accept invoices, but we need a mutual representation that the fallback is temporary and that Novaterra will provide the EU VAT registration details within X days. Otherwise Redwood US invoicing could create withholding or gross-up issues.
- Reverse-charge VAT: we can support reverse-charge invoices for EU-supplied services; we need Novaterra's VAT ID on the PO/invoice and a statement on the invoice that the buyer is liable for VAT under the reverse charge. We will also add the buyer VAT field as requested.
- Currency & net terms: Redwood prefers invoicing in EUR for EU customers; however we can invoice in USD if Novaterra prefers. Net terms: standard is Net 30; Ben — could we confirm Net 45 concession for this deal if Novaterra needs runway?

Next steps proposal: I'll send a one-page order form addendum that captures: (i) fallback billing-entity mechanics (temporary fallback, notification window, tax evidence), (ii) reverse-charge invoice example text, (iii) PO & VAT field requirements, (iv) currency & net terms options.

If that suits, I'll push the addendum to DocuSign and paste the language into the order form PDF so procurement can see the redline.

Thanks, Rafael. Tax/Payments answers below and proposed language at the bottom.

Operational notes:
- Reverse-charge: Confirmed — Redwood can issue invoices with the reverse-charge statement. We require Novaterra's VAT number on the PO and will include a line: "VAT reverse charge applies per Article 194 VAT Directive; buyer liable for VAT."
- Fallback invoicing: We can accept the fallback to Redwood US as an operational exception, provided Novaterra signs a short temporary fallback addendum (see text below) and supplies evidence that EU registration is in process within 30 days. Redwood will re-issue invoices to the EU entity once registration is confirmed.
- Currency: We'll default to EUR for reporting; if invoiced in USD, Redwood will apply the exchange rate on invoice date and note FX on the invoice.
- Net terms: finance is willing to set Net 45 for this specific order if deal-level approval (Ben) signs off.

Proposed addendum language (suggested):

"Temporary Billing Entity Fallback": In the event Customer's designated EU invoicing entity is unable to accept tax-compliant invoices at signing, Customer authorizes Redwood US, Inc. to act as temporary invoicing entity for the amounts due under this Order Form for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days from the Effective Date ("Fallback Period"). Customer agrees to use commercially reasonable efforts to provide evidence of EU VAT registration within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date. Upon receipt of satisfactory evidence of EU registration, Redwood will reissue invoices to the Customer's EU entity and provide credit/debit adjustments as necessary. Customer will not be relieved of any tax reporting obligations; any withholding or gross-up responsibilities shall be the Customer's.

We will also include an example invoice stub in the addendum showing the buyer VAT field and the reverse-charge statement.
